name: The Maker Movement comes to teachers in Tanzania

content.title: The Maker Movement comes to teachers in Tanzania
content.summary: AKU-IED conducted two exciting material making workshops to support early years' literacy development for educators one in Turiani, a rural part of Tanzania set in the district of Morogoro - 360 km from Dar es Salaam,  and the other at the Aga Khan U

content.text: Can you teach at school with recycled plastic bottles, cardboard paper, plastic lids, and glue? Dr. Lillian Vikiru, Assistant Professor at AKU-IED EA and Dr. Susan Crichton, Visiting Professor to IED from the University of British Columbia, Canada have shown how readily available resources found in communities, even the most marginalized, can be used to develop resources to stimulate young children and their teachers. They conducted two exciting material making workshops to support early years' literacy development for educators one in Turiani, a rural part of Tanzania set in the district of Morogoro - 360 km from Dar es Salaam,  and the other at the Aga Khan University campus in Dar es Salaam. These workshops launched the Canada Africa Research Grant (CAREG) project - Leapfrogging Pedagogical Challenges: Using Appropriate Technology to Foster Innovations in Literacy for the Knowledge Age, a collaboration between the two universities. This project will work with teachers from rural Tanzania to design, create and try out in their own classrooms materials and through the development of innovative teaching and learning resources from locally available materials and technologies, prototypes for work with other teachers will be developed.

The workshop in Turiani labeled TANGRAM DAY included working with teachers on developing materials for various teaching purposes including understanding and teaching numeracy, oral literacy, spatial literacy and conceptual literacy. For example, the CPs worked in groups to create a narrative, prepare masks and act out the narrative, all to support the development of skills early reading.

The second workshop took place at the AKU-IED, EA campus and attracted over 80 participants for its event: Taking Making Into the Schools: Embracing the Maker Movement as a Way to Introduce Design Thinking and Innovation. The participants included the Institute's first and second year Master of Education students. The philosophy of the Maker Movement suggests that for children to survive and thrive in the 21st century, they must be adept in using the skills essential in the knowledge age.  These skills include design thinking, problem finding and solving, and creativity.  Incorporating these ideas, the session turned to be a very busy, hands-on, session that was fun and challenging.

These two very stimulating workshops really succeeded in getting CAREG of to a flying, productive and creative start.  Dr Lillian Vikuru, as PI, will lead the project at IED-EA, managing the research and scholarship of teaching activities.  Lillian will spend 3 months at the University of British Columbia with Dr. Susan Crichton later in 2014.  Susan, herself, has recently been honoured with an award in Teaching Excellence and Innovation for her 'maker movement' work at UBC, where she directs the Innovative Learning Centre.
